sections.h2: The 54EC route beats every AAA and AA alternative over five years

chart.title: Only BBB and A-rated paper beats 54EC bonds at their 5.25% coupon
chart.sub: Terminal value of a ₹50 lakh gain after five years, ₹ lakh. The top row is a hypothetical market-rate 54EC, not purchasable.
chart.source: Author's model; issuer boards for 54EC coupons; RBI Floating Rate Savings Bond 2020 (Taxable).

sections.means: The 54EC bonds end at ₹60.09 lakh, ahead of every AAA and AA alternative and the RBI's 8.05% bond, and only BBB and A-rated paper beats them.

sections.h2: A rival must earn 9.92% pre-tax over five years to match 54EC at a 30% slab

chart.title: A 30% slab lifts the five-year breakeven to 9.92%, from 8.74% at a 5% slab
chart.sub: Pre-tax yield an alternative must earn to match 54EC over five years, by marginal slab rate, %.
chart.source: Author's model, same assumptions as the terminal-value table.

sections.means: The breakeven rises with the slab rate, so 54EC is worth most to investors in the highest bracket.
sections.todo: Judge 54EC over its five-year lock-in only, since its edge over higher-yielding rivals shrinks on longer horizons.

sections.h2: Below-market coupons return ₹4.25 lakh of the ₹6.50 lakh exemption to issuers

chart.title: The investor keeps ₹2.25 lakh of the ₹6.50 lakh tax exemption
chart.sub: Tax forgone on a ₹50 lakh gain, split between the investor and the issuers, ₹ lakh.
chart.source: Author's calculation; 54EC coupon of 5.25% against the 7.46% AAA PSU market yield.

sections.means: Repricing 54EC at the 7.46% market rate lifts its terminal value from ₹60.09 lakh to ₹64.33 lakh, which is the ₹4.25 lakh cost of the below-market coupon.
sections.todo: Judge the exemption by the ₹2.25 lakh the investor keeps, not by the ₹6.50 lakh headline tax saving.
